steps.label: Why it matters
steps.sub: models in this course use log returns

code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

prices = pd.read_csv(
    "prices.csv", index_col="date", parse_dates=True
)["close"]

simple_returns = prices.pct_change()
log_returns = np.log(prices).diff()
caption: pct_change() gives simple returns; differencing log prices gives log returns.

code:
# log returns sum across periods
r_total = log_returns.sum()

# recover cumulative simple growth
cum_growth = np.exp(log_returns.cumsum())

# vs. multiplicative compounding of simple returns
cum_growth_alt = (1 + simple_returns).cumprod()
caption: Log returns compound by addition; simple returns compound by multiplication.

subtitle: Lesson 2 looks at why the raw closing price isn't the right number to compute returns from.
